system_overview: This specification models the Non-Blocking Atomic Commitment (NBAC) protocol with crash failures, based on Raynal's 1997 case study of agreement problems in distributed systems. The protocol allows N processes to agree on committing or aborting a distributed transaction. Each process votes YES or NO, and the group must reach a consistent decision. The protocol uses an unreliable failure detector that may nondeterministically report whether some process has crashed.
actors_and_components: The system consists of N processes (numbered 1 through N) that communicate via message passing. Each process independently votes, sends its vote to all others, receives votes, and decides to commit or abort. A failure detector provides each process with a (potentially unreliable) indication of whether any process has crashed. Processes can crash at any point, after which they take no further steps.
state_variables: The system tracks: (1) A program counter for each process, indicating its current phase: voting YES, voting NO, vote sent, decided to abort, decided to commit, or crashed. (2) A set of received messages for each process, where each message is a pair of a sender identifier and a vote value (YES or NO). (3) A global set of sent messages (pairs of sender and vote value) representing the messages available in the network. (4) A failure detector output for each process: a boolean indicating whether the process currently suspects some process has crashed.
initial_state: No messages have been sent (empty set). Each process starts with a nondeterministic initial vote of either YES or NO (its program counter is set to YES or NO accordingly). No process has received any messages (empty set for each). The failure detector output is nondeterministically initialized for each process.
actions: Each process can take one step per transition, consisting of receiving messages, updating the failure detector, and performing one of these actions: (1) Vote YES: If the process's current state is YES, it sends a YES message (adds the pair of its identifier and YES to the sent set) and moves to the sent state. (2) Vote NO: If the process's current state is NO, it sends a NO message and moves to the sent state. (3) Crash: A non-crashed process moves to the crashed state. No new messages are sent. (4) Decide after sending: If the process has sent its vote, it evaluates: (a) If the failure detector reports a suspected crash, the process aborts. (b) If any received message contains a NO vote, the process aborts. (c) If the failure detector reports no suspected crash AND the process has received YES votes from all N processes, the process commits. (5) Do nothing: The process does not change state (to avoid deadlock when no other action is enabled). Message reception is modeled as nondeterministically selecting a subset of sent messages that includes all previously received messages. The failure detector nondeterministically updates its output at each step.
safety_properties: Type invariant: Sent messages are pairs of process identifiers and vote values. Program counters are in the valid state set. Received sets are subsets of valid message pairs. Failure detector outputs are booleans. Validity: If some process initially voted NO, then no process ever commits.
additional_assumptions: Weak fairness is assumed on the combined action of receiving messages plus voting (YES or NO) or deciding, ensuring that non-crashed processes eventually make progress. Crash transitions are not subject to fairness. The failure detector is completely nondeterministic in this specification -- it may switch between suspecting and not suspecting at each step. An alternative initial state where all processes vote YES is also defined but not used as the main specification.
